title: Analog Devices (ADI) Q4 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
transcript:
Management outlines a new reporting structure and rising capital spending plans.

ByMotley Fool Transcribing–Nov 24, 2026 at 4:08PM EST

Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

TAKEAWAYS

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email[email protected]

RISKS

SUMMARY

Analog Devices(ADI-17.37%)reported record annual performance driven by growth across all end markets and expansion in AI-related infrastructure. Management stated that while AI infrastructure investments fueled data center and test equipment demand, more than two-thirds of total growth originated from non-AI-centric markets. The company indicated that it is increasing capital investments to address manufacturing constraints and expand its technology portfolio through acquisitions like Alif Semiconductor. Management also announced a change in end-market reporting to provide greater visibility into the data center business.

INDUSTRY GLOSSARY

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator:Morning, and welcome to the Analog Devices Fourth Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Earnings Conference Call, which is being audio webcast via telephone and over the web. I'd now like to introduce your host for today's call, Mr. Jeff Ambrosi, Head of Investor Relations. Sir, the floor is yours.

Jeff Ambrosi:Thank you, Danny, and good morning, everybody. Thank you for joining our fourth quarter fiscal 2026 conference call. Joining me today is ADI's CEO and Chair, Vincent T. Roche, and ADI's CFO, Richard C. Puccio Jr.. Before we begin, I'd like to highlight an upcoming change to how we present revenue by end market. Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Data Center will be reported as a standalone end market, and our revenue from our wireless business will be reported within Industrial, which also includes revenue from Aerospace and Defense, Automation, Test and Measurement, Healthcare, and Energy applications. Automotive and Consumer will be unchanged.

This change only affects how we present revenue by end market and does not change our segment reporting or total reported revenue. In connection with our first quarter fiscal 2027 results in February, we will publish three years of recast quarterly revenue by end market on our investor relations website. Now, for anyone who missed our earnings release, you can find it at investor.analog.com, along with related financial schedules. The information we're about to discuss includes forward-looking statements, which are subject to certain risks and uncertainties, as further described in our earnings release, periodic reports, and other materials filed with the SEC.

Actual results could differ materially from the forward-looking information, as these statements reflect our expectations only as of the date of this call. We undertake no obligation to update these statements, except as required by law. References to gross margin, operating and non-operating expenses, operating margin, tax rate, earnings per share, and free cash flow in our comments today will be on a non-GAAP basis, which excludes special items. When comparing our results to our historical performance, special items are also excluded from prior periods. Reconciliations of these non-GAAP measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures and additional information about our non-GAAP measures are included in today's earnings release.

References to earnings per share are on a fully diluted basis. With that, I will turn the call over to ADI CEO and Chair, Vincent T. Roche.

Vincent T. Roche:Thank you, Jeff, and a very good morning to each and every one of you. Capping off a record year for ADI, fourth quarter revenue, margin, and earnings all came in above the midpoint of our guidance. For the full year, our revenue increased nearly 40% to more than $15 billion, with robust double-digit growth across all of our end markets. AI infrastructure-driven investments drove significant growth for both our ATE and Data Center businesses. That said, more than two-thirds of our total growth was driven by non-AI-centric markets, highlighting the diversity of our customer base and our ability to capitalize on numerous secular tailwinds, as well as the broader cyclical recovery.

Our fiscal 2026 top-line growth was paired with significant margin expansion, which enabled us to deliver record free cash flow of $5.5 billion. We attribute these results to the optionality and resiliency of our business model, long-term commitment to innovation and customer success, and strong operational execution right across the company. As our customers tackle ever more difficult challenges at the boundary between the physical and digital worlds, we believe we are well-positioned to deliver and capture even greater value in the future. As we have long said, R&D is our first call on capital because innovation is the wellspring of ADI's value creation.

Our R&D investments in fiscal 2026 were the largest in our history, spanning analog, digital, software, and AI. We also continued ramping investments to enhance our customers' end-to-end experience of ADI from ideation to realization. On the M&A side, our acquisition of Alif added AI-native microcontrollers and fusion processors to our AI toolbox. In addition, our acquisition of Empower strengthens our ability to grow the core power market, which we view as one of the largest SAM opportunities within AI infrastructure. Taken together, these investments significantly expanded our ability to solve increasingly complex challenges for our customers, delivering more complete solutions, combining cutting-edge sensing, signal processing, connectivity, and power.

We credit this overall investment strategy for our record design and pipeline growth of 40% this past year, eclipsing our FY 2025 record, with contributions across all end markets and regions. Our robust customer pipeline is more than a leading indicator of future revenue, however. We believe it reflects the growing criticality of our solutions in the AI era, as rapid technological evolution creates ever more complex challenges across numerous and different markets. Customers are increasingly turning to ADI's higher-value offerings to help lower their total cost of ownership, accelerate their time to market, and, of course, enhance system performance. Our differentiated value is reflected in ADI's average selling prices, which are more than 4x the industry average.

The ASPs of our newer products are notably higher, reflecting the increasing value of our solutions that we are delivering to our customers. I would like to spend the remainder of my planned remarks sharing how we are translating innovation into growth for ADI across the various market sectors, beginning with our industrial business, which comprises test and measurement, automation, aerospace and defense, healthcare, and energy. Starting first, test and measurement. We are benefiting from the intensely demanding test requirements of modern AI compute, memory, networking, and power systems, where complexity is increasing at an extraordinary rate. This plays directly to ADI's leadership in high-performance signal intelligence that transforms raw physics into insight and response.

The greater accuracy, bandwidth, and measurement precision enabled by our technology helps customers test next-generation devices more rapidly, more efficiently, and with greater confidence. This resulted in record ATE and ETM revenue this year, and record design-ins that we believe position us for continued growth through fiscal 2027 and beyond. In industrial automation, customers continue to digitalize, automate, and deploy robots across semiconductor fabs, biopharma, data centers, and other manufacturing environments to accelerate productivity and address evolving geopolitical and labor dynamics. As a result, our automation revenue and design-ins across industrial control, connectivity, and robotics segments accelerated significantly in fiscal 2026, with the fastest growth coming from robotics.

We expect the next evolution of robotics from automation to autonomy will unlock tasks that historically required human intervention and create opportunity for higher-value ADI content and subsystems that can reduce latency and increase system accuracy. Autonomous robotic modalities, including humanoids, which can require up to 10x more ADI content compared to traditional robots, will steadily increase our opportunity over time. In aerospace and defense, systems are evolving rapidly to sense threats earlier, communicate securely in contested environments, and make mission-critical decisions much, much faster. These requirements are driving increasingly complex radar, communications, and autonomous machines, where ADI's ability to combine RF, signal processing, IMUs, and power management into higher-value solutions is differentiated.

In this sector, we almost doubled growth in our design pipeline this past year across both established and emerging defense customers, which we believe positions us for continued growth in 2027 and beyond. In healthcare, our revenue growth accelerated in 2026 as innovation across the industry increasingly converged around continuous glucose monitoring, AI-assisted imaging, and surgical robotics. Our precision sensing, signal processing, algorithms, and ultra-low-power technologies are helping customers to deliver innovative solutions designed to better manage chronic disease, help clinicians detect and diagnose conditions earlier, and make complex procedures more precise and less invasive. Our growing design and pipeline across myriad applications there positions ADI for continued growth in fiscal 2027 and reinforces the potential of our longer-term opportunity.

In energy, rapidly rising electricity demand is magnifying one of the world's most fundamental engineering challenges: how to generate, manage, store, and deliver significantly more power while improving efficiency and reliability. ADI sits at several key points across that system. For example, our precision sensing enables greater visibility and control of the grid, while our battery management technologies enable more efficient storage and local distribution. Energy was one of our strongest areas of pipeline growth through fiscal 2026, reinforcing our long-term outlook for this business. Turning now to automotive, we delivered a second consecutive year of record revenue, despite lower vehicle production, due to our strong and expanding position in next-generation ADAS and infotainment systems.

As vehicles move toward greater autonomy, they must process dramatically more sensor information, move more data, and reliably power many interconnected subsystems, all the while meeting demanding requirements for signal integrity, energy efficiency, and safety. These challenges play to ADI's strengths in high-speed connectivity and power solutions designed to support functional safety requirements. L2+ autonomous driving systems remain relatively early in their global adoption, and as the industry progresses toward higher levels of autonomy, we expect content opportunities for ADI to continue to increase. In the past year, design and growth across our GMSL, A2B, and functionally safe power solutions underscores our substantial role in enabling the vehicle of tomorrow.

We saw a strong increase in designs for battery management solutions, which we expect to grow in the coming year and beyond as EV adoption increases. Not surprisingly, our data center business was our fastest-growing market in fiscal 2026, both from a revenue and design-in perspective. Robust investments in AI infrastructure are creating enormous challenges around two of the physical bottlenecks to scaling AI: moving exponentially more data and efficiently delivering unprecedented power loads. ADI is well-positioned to address both. In the networking domain, our optical control technology keeps electro-optical systems precisely tuned across everything from pluggables to OCS, so that every packet of light is accurate, stable, and efficient.

As you know, data center power has become one of the most significant constraints to AI advancement, as increasing rack and processor densities are fundamentally changing how power is converted, controlled, protected, and delivered. Customers are choosing ADI to help ensure that every watt used in the data center is available for computation and maximum impact. As the resulting thermodynamic challenges grow with increasing power density, liquid cooling is shifting from an option to a requirement. Customers are turning to ADI to translate physical signals, such as temperature, flow, leakage, and coolant health, into actionable intelligence, which is creating a new differentiated content opportunity.

Overall, we believe our data center revenues will continue to be one of the faster-growing businesses in 2027 and beyond. Finally, continued demand at the premium end of the consumer market overcame memory headwinds to drive double-digit growth in revenue and design activity across premium handsets, wearables, hearables, and gaming segments, which positions ADI for continued diversified growth in this sector in 2027 and beyond. In closing, FY 2026 demonstrated what makes ADI different. We are built to define and capture new waves of opportunity as we compound the businesses underpinning our resilience through cycles.

We leverage a six-decade culture of curiosity and cutting-edge innovation to continuously advance the state of the art at the electrophysical interface, a boundary that is increasingly central to the advance of technology's most valuable applications. Our customers increasingly choose ADI as a strategic partner for our applications, domain expertise, scope of high-performance analog software and AI capabilities, and differentiated hybrid manufacturing strategy. As we enter 2027, we continue to invest with discipline to further enhance and extend the value we can deliver to our customers and shareholders alike in the years ahead. With that, I'll turn it over to Rich.

Richard C. Puccio Jr.:Thank you, Vince, and let me add my welcome to our fourth quarter earnings call. I'll start with a brief overview of our full year fiscal 2026 financial performance. Revenue for the year came in at $15.2 billion, up 38% from fiscal 2025, reflecting broad-based strength across the business. Gross margin finished at 72.9%, up 360 basis points, driven by mix, utilization, and higher revenue. Operating margin finished at 49.5%, up 760 basis points, reflecting gross margin fall-through and strong operating leverage. Earnings per share increased 68% to $13.05. Turning to the fourth quarter, revenue came in toward the high end of our outlook at $4.37 billion, growing 9% sequentially and 42% year-over-year.

Industrial represented 50% of our fourth quarter revenue, finishing up 11% sequentially and 55% year-over-year. Ongoing cyclical momentum, along with secular demand in the AI infrastructure and defense markets, resulted in broad-based growth, including record results in aerospace and defense, ATE, and electronic test and measurement. For the full year, industrial grew 51%, reflecting the depth and breadth of our business, with all of our industrial sectors seeing accelerating double-digit growth. Aerospace and defense, ATE, and electronic test and measurement reached new highs for the year. Automotive represented 24% of quarterly revenue, finishing up 5% sequentially and 21% year-over-year.

We saw continued growth for our leading connectivity, audio processing, and power solutions, as well as a notable pickup in demand for our battery management systems. For the full year, automotive increased by 12%, driven by continued content and share gains in next-generation ADAS and infotainment systems, despite the backdrop of lower vehicle sales. Additionally, BMS revenue returned to full-year growth after two years of decline. Communications represented 16% of quarterly revenue, finishing up 8% sequentially and 81% year-over-year. Our data center business now represents 83% of comms, or 13% of total sales, growing more than 100% year-on-year for the second consecutive quarter, fueled by AI-driven demand.

Wireless revenue was up double digits year over year for the fifth straight quarter. For the full year, communications increased 74% and was our fastest-growing market for a second consecutive year, reflecting our growing presence in AI infrastructure and a cyclical recovery in wireless. Consumer represented 10% of quarterly revenue, finishing up 7% sequentially and year over year, remaining resilient in the face of memory-related headwinds. For the full year, consumer increased 15%, with all applications growing double digits, driven by our exposure to high-end handsets, secularly growing wearables and hearables, and a notable acceleration in our prosumer business. Now on to the rest of the P&L.

Fourth quarter gross margin was 74.5%, up 200 basis points sequentially and 470 basis points year over year, driven predominantly by favorable mix and higher revenue. OpEx in the quarter was $972 million, resulting in an operating margin of 52.3%, up 230 basis points sequentially and 880 basis points year over year. Non-operating expenses finished at $37 million, lower than expected due to mark-to-market gains from strategic balance sheet investments. Our tax rate for the quarter was 12.3%. EPS was $4.06, up 18% sequentially and 80% year over year. Now I'd like to highlight a few items from our balance sheet and cash flow statements.

Cash and short-term investments finished the quarter at $5.2 billion, and our net leverage ratio decreased slightly to 0.8x. As planned, we built strategic die bank and finished goods buffers throughout the quarter. Inventory increased $152 million sequentially, with days of inventory increasing to 165. Channel inventory also increased as we are now back within our six to seven-week model. The investments we have made in inventory over the past two years have helped drive sustained above-seasonal growth and mitigate lead time expansion, especially for certain products where demand is exceeding supply. Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow was $6.2 billion, and CapEx was $0.7 billion, resulting in free cash flow of $5.5 billion, or 36% of revenue.

Over the same period, we returned $5.4 billion to shareholders via dividends and share repurchase, in line with our commitment to return 100% of free cash flow over the long term. Now moving on to our first quarter 2027 outlook. Revenue is expected to be $4.4 billion, ± $150 million. Operating margin at the midpoint is expected to be 50.5%, ±100 basis points. Non-operating expense is expected to be roughly $90 million. Our tax rate is expected to be 12%-14%, and based on these inputs, adjusted EPS is expected to be $3.82, ±$0.20. Turning to capital investment.

We have executed well against our manufacturing expansion plans laid out at our Investor Day in 2022, building the capacity to support the high end of our 7%-10% long-term growth model. We are also well-positioned from a capacity standpoint to support sustained above-seasonal growth through fiscal 2027. Looking past 2027, while considering our momentum and the strong pipeline execution Vince referenced earlier, our confidence in future growth has risen. In order to capitalize on our potential, we are expanding our capacity further and currently expect fiscal 2027 CapEx to be approximately $1.6 billion-$1.9 billion.

Even with this higher investment, we expect fiscal 2027 free cash flow to increase meaningfully, and our commitment to return 100% of free cash flow over the long term is unchanged. In closing, fiscal 2026 caps one of the strongest growth years in ADI's history. We achieved record revenue, profitability, and earnings per share while generating more than $5 billion of free cash flow. We achieved these results while continuing to invest in the businesses and the innovation that we believe will fuel our future success. As we look ahead, we believe we are well-positioned to build on this momentum, supported by the strength of our business model and our track record of disciplined operational execution.

With that, I'll give it back to Jeff for Q&A.

Jeff Ambrosi:Thank you, Rich. Now let's get to our Q&A session. We ask that you limit yourself to one question in order to allow for additional participants on the call this morning. If you have a follow-up, please re-queue, and we'll take your question if time allows. With that, operator, can we have our first question, please?

Operator:For those participating by telephone dial-in, if you have a question, please press star one on your phone to enter the queue. If your question has been answered and you wish to be removed from the queue, please press star one again. If you're listening on a speakerphone, please pick up the handset when asking your question. In the interest of time, we ask that you please limit yourself to one question. We'll pause for just a moment to compile the Q&A roster. Our first question comes from Tore Svanberg with Stifel. Your line is open.

Tore Svanberg:Yes, thank you, and congratulations on the strong results. Vince, there's a lot of sort of macro issues and concerns out there. You sound very confident. Rich just talked about increasing CapEx next year. I think he also said you expect to grow above seasonal throughout fiscal 2027. So, help us sort of level set what's going on here between some of the perhaps noise at the macro level and what you're seeing, because it does feel like you're actually seeing continuous growth above your long-term target, certainly in fiscal 2027, maybe even in 2028 as well.

Vincent T. Roche:Yeah. Thanks, Tore. So, yeah, I think, at a high level, the opportunity that ADI is addressing has been growing in leaps and bounds. As you know, we address many, many different applications. Our span is very, very strong, actually, across all the regions of the world. We've got, I would say, at this point in time, a broader set of some very significant secular drivers. We're not dependent on just a very concentrated infrastructure data center buildout. Generally as well, if I look at the ASP structures of the company right now, they reflect our ability to generate value beyond what our competitors can do and capture that value.

But also, if I look at the new products in our pipeline, the products that we're bringing to market now, some of these products have very, very significant multiples over the older generation products. I think in terms of the intersection of many markets in which we have increasing strength, our ability to support the old legacy products with increasing ASPs, newer products with much higher ASPs. And what we pay a lot of attention to, Tore, is the pipeline. I mean, what do the order books tell us? Well, the order books tell us right now that POS bookings are significantly higher than POS billings.

And our customer wins in terms of our design and pipeline right across all the sectors, and I mentioned many of them in the earnings script here, are at a record level. In fact, our 2026 pipeline has compounded significantly beyond an already strong 2025 pipeline, which grew significantly beyond 2024. You put all those things together, I see, for example, also in the world of AI, we're at the beginning of the buildout of a very, very significant meta-technology that will change all other technologies. So, we'll continue to unpack that story for you as time progresses. But I'd say we've got a lot of idiosyncratic secular tailwinds and cyclical, particularly in the industrial market.

Tore Svanberg:Thank you.

Jeff Ambrosi:Thanks, Tore. And just to clarify, Richard's comment on, it was a capacity statement on being able to support above seasonal growth. It wasn't guidance for the year for fiscal 2027. We'll take our next caller, please.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question comes from Vivek Arya with Bank of America Securities. Your line is open.

Vivek Arya:Thanks for taking my questions. Actually, both related to just the near-term outlook. You are guiding the current quarter sort of flattish. It seems a little conservative relative, I think, when it's to several quarters of above seasonal growth. I am just curious, would you call this kind of seasonal, below seasonal? Just what you are seeing from a sequential segment perspective. And then one for, kind of related, for Rich on operating margins. I think you are guiding down 200 basis points almost sequentially. Just what are the puts and takes of gross margin and OpEx, and is there some indication there of how we should think about those metrics trending into 2027? That would be incredibly helpful.

Thank you.

Vincent T. Roche:Sure. Rich, why don't you?

Richard C. Puccio Jr.:Thanks, Vivek. I will start with your first question around the seasonality. But first, just as a backdrop, the upside to our Q4 midpoint was driven heavily by the industrial and automotive, while comms was a little bit weaker, driven by some sequential softness in the wireless piece. Data center, however, was as expected and was up double digits sequentially, and consumer was as expected. Now, if we look out at the Q1 market outlook, as we have guided, we are expecting it to grow modestly quarter over quarter, which actually is well above our Q1 seasonality. Typically, our Q1 would be down mid-single digits. So, I do think that we are guiding a strong above seasonal first quarter.

From an end market perspective, we expect communications to be up mid-single digits, obviously being led by the data center growth. Industrial is expected to be up low mid-single digits. Auto expected to be down low single digits, and consumer down 10%-15%. The other thing I would tell you is we would expect channel inventory to stay flattish, with weeks likely to fall. That is how I feel about our guide from a revenue perspective. On the gross margin side, obviously we came in better than expected, driven by higher revenue and favorable mix.

As I mentioned, I think I talked about this in last quarter's call, we shut down our fabs around the holidays, which we will do again this year. As a result, we see gross margin in Q1 moderating down to approximately 74%. If we flip forward as we work our way down to the Op margin piece, obviously we delivered a significant amount of leverage in fiscal 2026. Q4 operating margin was about 30 bps above midpoint of our guidance, almost entirely driven by gross margin favorability, as expenses were a bit higher than planned, driven by sales commissions.

We are also leaning in, as we have talked about, into AI and driving a little bit higher token and cloud costs in that period. When we look at Q1, we are anticipating OpEx to grow in the mid-single digits sequentially, driven by our continued growth in our investments. We will also have a full year, sorry, a full quarter of Alif Semiconductor in our expenses, which obviously puts some upward pressure on the expense. However, and I think it is an important point, for the year, we continue to target OpEx growth at roughly half of the rate of revenue growth, and we do see continued operating leverage for the full year.

Jeff Ambrosi:Thank you, Vivek. Take our next caller, please.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question comes from James (Jim) Schneider with Goldman Sachs. Your line is open.

James (Jim) Schneider:Good morning. Thanks for taking my question. With respect to the CapEx investments you're making to expand capacity, can you maybe give us a sense, once those investments have been made this year, what revenue level you can support with the new capacity? Then maybe separately speak to any kind of constraints or bottlenecks you're seeing on the foundry side for those products which are made external to ADI. Thank you.

Richard C. Puccio Jr.:Thanks, Jim. First, a couple of starter points. The billion-dollar step-up essentially that I talked about in 2027 versus 2026, one important point is a chunk of that will be eligible for meaningful tax credits under the CHIPS Act. We will get some offset in our depreciation going forward and also get some offset in the amount of cash flow net that goes out the door. The way to think about the investment we're making, big piece of it is going to go towards clean room expansion at our European and U.S. sites. These are places where we already have available space within existing fabs, and we're also investing in back-end test and assembly capacity.

I do expect CapEx for these projects will decline as we move into 2028, and that will put us back down into our long-term CapEx model of 4%-6% of revenue. I do expect that we'll start to see some of the new capacity come online in stages, starting as early as, for us, Q1 2028, which gives us significantly more supply for our highest demand nodes and products. Obviously, really important positioning us for sustained future growth. I would say from a constraints perspective, frankly, I think it's tight everywhere. It's tight in internal fabs, back-end, OSAT, foundry. Right now, it's an industry-wide dynamic.

I would say for us, we're working really hard to sort of de-bottleneck and unlock incremental supply everywhere we can. I think I've talked in prior quarters that essentially on a weekly basis, we're adding incremental capability and capacity as tools are coming online from purchases we started making upwards of nine months ago, just to give some perspective on how long the team has been working on building up supply. Obviously, we've been able to demonstrate what we've been doing there with our ability to supply above seasonal demand throughout this past year, and we expect we can continue to do the same into 2027.

Vincent T. Roche:Yeah, just a couple of additional pieces of color. I think certainly over the past six months or so, I would say packaging, assembly has been the primary choke point. Solving that problem obviously is much easier than solving a fab problem just in terms of the timescales it takes to bring equipment into the manufacturing process. But we see that improving with each passing month. The other thing I just want to talk about to add a little color to what Rich has said about CapEx, we've always been very disciplined in how we spend our CapEx. Obviously, many, many times we've talked about our hybrid manufacturing model. Most of the silicon we procure is from external partners.

That will remain the case in the years ahead. But we're adding capacity on very, very specific processes inside the company where we need to build more resiliency, extend our footprint for many, many of our core markets. And those of you who've known us for a long time know that our behavior is to invest in stages in line with demand. That's what I think you can expect in the years ahead in what I believe is a growth inflection for the industry and for ADI.

Jeff Ambrosi:Thank you, Jim. We'll take our next question, please.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question comes from Harlan Sur with J.P. Morgan. Your line is open.

Harlan Sur:Yeah, good morning. Thanks for taking my question. Vince gave us a great summary of the industrial segment drivers going forward, and I know the team has always talked about the potential for more incremental gross margin upside as your higher margin broad market industrial business drives back to sort of historical consumption levels. I seem to recall that last quarter, broad market industrial was still sort of double digits percentage below historical consumption levels. So where are your broad market shipments currently trending as the cyclical dynamics have continued to improve?

And as that continues to move higher, can that drive another, let's say, 100+ basis points of gross margin upside from a 74% level over the next few quarters?

Vincent T. Roche:Rich, you want to take that one, and then I'll add some color as necessary?

Richard C. Puccio Jr.:Sure. So, I'm going to try to unpack that a little bit, Harlan. First talking about this notion of where we are relative to consumption. I think it is, and obviously this consumption we're talking about is the sort of longer-term growth trend line. Clearly, if you look at our overall numbers, revenue finished well above that trend line for 2026, after having been well under in 2024 and 2025. I'll break it down because I do think this is important as we think about where we are in this cycle.

Driving the above consumption trend line in 2026 was our aerospace and defense business, our ATE business, and our data center businesses, which are continuing to achieve significant new highs with continued momentum, right? That's about 30% of our revenue. We believe the strength in these markets are driven by better end demand, not inventory restocking. As for the rest of our businesses, we believe we are shipping either to or below consumption today. Essentially, outside of that 30% chunk of our business, we are still below the long-term trend line. Overall, we feel good about where we are from a shipment level relative to trend.

The other thing is we do not see any evidence yet of any material restocking across our customer portfolio.

Vincent T. Roche:Yeah, so I think your assertion, Harlan, that with the continued improvement in kind of the broad fragmented market, we will see margin improvement. I cannot give you a number, but we know that will be directionally true.

Richard C. Puccio Jr.:Yeah, and following on to that, you can see it in our numbers. We finished with 50% of our business in industrial, and I have been talking about this track for a while. Every percentage point we grow industrial as a share gives us some opportunity for some gross margin appreciation. As a reminder, we have talked about this now for a couple quarters, given where we are running and the supply constraints that we have talked about, utilization is not going to be a driver for us over the near to medium term for improved gross margin. It will continue to be revenue acceleration and mix, and mix within the mix, obviously.

So, continued growth, you are right, the continued growth in industrial and gaining share of our overall revenue will give us opportunity for appreciation.

Jeff Ambrosi:Thank you, Harlan.

Harlan Sur:Great, thank you.

Jeff Ambrosi:Thanks, Harlan. Take the next question, please.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question comes from Joshua Buchalter with TD Cowen. Your line is open.

Joshua Buchalter:Hey, guys. Thank you for taking my question, and congrats on the very strong year. I wanted to ask about the comm segment specifically and double-click a bit there. I totally realize the year-over-year growth is fantastic, but can you maybe walk us through again the drivers of what the sequential deceleration? I know you called out wireless being weaker, but I think that was only supposed to be around less than 20% of revenue now, with data center +80%. Any metrics you can give us on sort of the underlying business underneath within comms, whether across power or optical in data center? Thank you.

Richard C. Puccio Jr.:Yeah, thanks, Josh. You're right. I think what I said was that the data center part of comms was up to 87% and only-- Sorry, 83%, and the rest is in the wireless. I'll give you the breakdown, and then I'll talk about the split, which is, I think, what you want to hear. Data center obviously continues to hit new highs, up more than 100% year-over-year again in Q4. Remains our strongest business from a growth perspective. Book to bill continued as being nicely above 1x, and signals from our pipeline indicate a strong long-term trajectory. As Vince mentioned, design-in and design-win results in data center have been very strong.

If you look for the year, data center was up more than 90%. Optical did grow a bit faster than power, which is a little bit of a shift. We had been talking about power and optical growing about the same, but we did see a little bit faster growth in optical. For fiscal 2027, we only guide one quarter, but I do feel confident that data center, both power and optical, will have significant growth for us in fiscal 2027. On the other piece, just quickly on wireless, as we're talking about comms in a current construct, we've mentioned it'll roll up into industrial next quarter.

We continue to benefit from the cyclical recovery, and while we saw some moderation in Q4, it has continued to grow double digits year-over-year for five quarters.

Joshua Buchalter:Thank you for the[crosstalk].

Jeff Ambrosi:Yeah, Josh, just to add quickly on data center. Last quarter, I think we talked about it being up 10% sequentially. It was a bit better than that sequentially. Vincent T. Roche:Yeah, I'd say, Stacy, the way to think about the data center business. It behaves a lot like a B2B business. It is driven by performance. It's highly diversified. The number of products, the number of SKUs we sell across the various parts of the data center and cloud business is quite diverse. It behaves a lot like a B2B sector.

Jeff Ambrosi:Thank you. Operator, we'll take our last question, please.

Operator:Thank you. Our final question comes from Matthew Prisco with Cantor. Your line is open.

Matthew Prisco:Hey, guys. Thanks for taking the question. Maybe you can walk us through the cyclical backdrop a little bit more as you see it today. Linearity of orders through the quarter, escalation trends, backlog, lead times, visibility, kind of all that good stuff. Richard C. Puccio Jr.:[crosstalk] Yeah, I'll take that. Okay, so I'll start with the cycle, sort of our thoughts on when does it end and where are we now, right? You can see that in our order book and our pipeline and our overall assessment of our inventories. Also, we've talked a lot about the auto share gains, where we've been very successful in the next-gen ADAS and infotainment, particularly in the fastest-growing car market, China EVs. In fact, we got closer to $900 million in synergies in 2026, and we expect we will exceed our billion-dollar target easily in 2027.

If you look at what we are seeing from a bookings perspective and a book-to-bill, as we talked about before, momentum here is ongoing. We can see it in the breadth and strength of the demand. On the indirect side, channel, as we mentioned, we have been working hard to get more inventory into the channel, had fallen below the six-week mark, and have now gotten ourselves back up into the six-to-seven-week target. We feel like we are still pretty lean from an inventory perspective in the channel. Demand is still strong. Cancellation activities are pretty normal. SUMMARY

Analog Devices(ADI-17.37%)reported record annual performance driven by growth across all end markets and expansion in AI-related infrastructure. Management stated that while AI infrastructure investments fueled data center and test equipment demand, more than two-thirds of total growth originated from non-AI-centric markets. The company indicated that it is increasing capital investments to address manufacturing constraints and expand its technology portfolio through acquisitions like Alif Semiconductor. Management also announced a change in end-market reporting to provide greater visibility into the data center business.

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator:Morning, and welcome to the Analog Devices Fourth Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Earnings Conference Call, which is being audio webcast via telephone and over the web. I'd now like to introduce your host for today's call, Mr. Jeff Ambrosi, Head of Investor Relations. Sir, the floor is yours.

Jeff Ambrosi:Thank you, Danny, and good morning, everybody. Thank you for joining our fourth quarter fiscal 2026 conference call. Joining me today is ADI's CEO and Chair, Vincent T. Roche, and ADI's CFO, Richard C. Puccio Jr.. Before we begin, I'd like to highlight an upcoming change to how we present revenue by end market. Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Data Center will be reported as a standalone end market, and our revenue from our wireless business will be reported within Industrial, which also includes revenue from Aerospace and Defense, Automation, Test and Measurement, Healthcare, and Energy applications. Automotive and Consumer will be unchanged.

This change only affects how we present revenue by end market and does not change our segment reporting or total reported revenue. In connection with our first quarter fiscal 2027 results in February, we will publish three years of recast quarterly revenue by end market on our investor relations website. Now, for anyone who missed our earnings release, you can find it at investor.analog.com, along with related financial schedules. The information we're about to discuss includes forward-looking statements, which are subject to certain risks and uncertainties, as further described in our earnings release, periodic reports, and other materials filed with the SEC.

Actual results could differ materially from the forward-looking information, as these statements reflect our expectations only as of the date of this call. We undertake no obligation to update these statements, except as required by law. References to gross margin, operating and non-operating expenses, operating margin, tax rate, earnings per share, and free cash flow in our comments today will be on a non-GAAP basis, which excludes special items. When comparing our results to our historical performance, special items are also excluded from prior periods. Reconciliations of these non-GAAP measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures and additional information about our non-GAAP measures are included in today's earnings release.

References to earnings per share are on a fully diluted basis. With that, I will turn the call over to ADI CEO and Chair, Vincent T. Roche.

Vincent T. Roche:Thank you, Jeff, and a very good morning to each and every one of you. Capping off a record year for ADI, fourth quarter revenue, margin, and earnings all came in above the midpoint of our guidance. For the full year, our revenue increased nearly 40% to more than $15 billion, with robust double-digit growth across all of our end markets. AI infrastructure-driven investments drove significant growth for both our ATE and Data Center businesses. That said, more than two-thirds of our total growth was driven by non-AI-centric markets, highlighting the diversity of our customer base and our ability to capitalize on numerous secular tailwinds, as well as the broader cyclical recovery.

Our fiscal 2026 top-line growth was paired with significant margin expansion, which enabled us to deliver record free cash flow of $5.5 billion. We attribute these results to the optionality and resiliency of our business model, long-term commitment to innovation and customer success, and strong operational execution right across the company. As our customers tackle ever more difficult challenges at the boundary between the physical and digital worlds, we believe we are well-positioned to deliver and capture even greater value in the future. As we have long said, R&D is our first call on capital because innovation is the wellspring of ADI's value creation.

Our R&D investments in fiscal 2026 were the largest in our history, spanning analog, digital, software, and AI. We also continued ramping investments to enhance our customers' end-to-end experience of ADI from ideation to realization. On the M&A side, our acquisition of Alif added AI-native microcontrollers and fusion processors to our AI toolbox. In addition, our acquisition of Empower strengthens our ability to grow the core power market, which we view as one of the largest SAM opportunities within AI infrastructure. Taken together, these investments significantly expanded our ability to solve increasingly complex challenges for our customers, delivering more complete solutions, combining cutting-edge sensing, signal processing, connectivity, and power.

We credit this overall investment strategy for our record design and pipeline growth of 40% this past year, eclipsing our FY 2025 record, with contributions across all end markets and regions. Our robust customer pipeline is more than a leading indicator of future revenue, however. We believe it reflects the growing criticality of our solutions in the AI era, as rapid technological evolution creates ever more complex challenges across numerous and different markets. Customers are increasingly turning to ADI's higher-value offerings to help lower their total cost of ownership, accelerate their time to market, and, of course, enhance system performance. Our differentiated value is reflected in ADI's average selling prices, which are more than 4x the industry average.

The ASPs of our newer products are notably higher, reflecting the increasing value of our solutions that we are delivering to our customers. I would like to spend the remainder of my planned remarks sharing how we are translating innovation into growth for ADI across the various market sectors, beginning with our industrial business, which comprises test and measurement, automation, aerospace and defense, healthcare, and energy. Starting first, test and measurement. We are benefiting from the intensely demanding test requirements of modern AI compute, memory, networking, and power systems, where complexity is increasing at an extraordinary rate. This plays directly to ADI's leadership in high-performance signal intelligence that transforms raw physics into insight and response.

The greater accuracy, bandwidth, and measurement precision enabled by our technology helps customers test next-generation devices more rapidly, more efficiently, and with greater confidence. This resulted in record ATE and ETM revenue this year, and record design-ins that we believe position us for continued growth through fiscal 2027 and beyond. In industrial automation, customers continue to digitalize, automate, and deploy robots across semiconductor fabs, biopharma, data centers, and other manufacturing environments to accelerate productivity and address evolving geopolitical and labor dynamics. As a result, our automation revenue and design-ins across industrial control, connectivity, and robotics segments accelerated significantly in fiscal 2026, with the fastest growth coming from robotics.

We expect the next evolution of robotics from automation to autonomy will unlock tasks that historically required human intervention and create opportunity for higher-value ADI content and subsystems that can reduce latency and increase system accuracy. Autonomous robotic modalities, including humanoids, which can require up to 10x more ADI content compared to traditional robots, will steadily increase our opportunity over time. In aerospace and defense, systems are evolving rapidly to sense threats earlier, communicate securely in contested environments, and make mission-critical decisions much, much faster. These requirements are driving increasingly complex radar, communications, and autonomous machines, where ADI's ability to combine RF, signal processing, IMUs, and power management into higher-value solutions is differentiated.

In this sector, we almost doubled growth in our design pipeline this past year across both established and emerging defense customers, which we believe positions us for continued growth in 2027 and beyond. In healthcare, our revenue growth accelerated in 2026 as innovation across the industry increasingly converged around continuous glucose monitoring, AI-assisted imaging, and surgical robotics. Our precision sensing, signal processing, algorithms, and ultra-low-power technologies are helping customers to deliver innovative solutions designed to better manage chronic disease, help clinicians detect and diagnose conditions earlier, and make complex procedures more precise and less invasive. Our growing design and pipeline across myriad applications there positions ADI for continued growth in fiscal 2027 and reinforces the potential of our longer-term opportunity.

In energy, rapidly rising electricity demand is magnifying one of the world's most fundamental engineering challenges: how to generate, manage, store, and deliver significantly more power while improving efficiency and reliability. ADI sits at several key points across that system. For example, our precision sensing enables greater visibility and control of the grid, while our battery management technologies enable more efficient storage and local distribution. Energy was one of our strongest areas of pipeline growth through fiscal 2026, reinforcing our long-term outlook for this business. Turning now to automotive, we delivered a second consecutive year of record revenue, despite lower vehicle production, due to our strong and expanding position in next-generation ADAS and infotainment systems.

As vehicles move toward greater autonomy, they must process dramatically more sensor information, move more data, and reliably power many interconnected subsystems, all the while meeting demanding requirements for signal integrity, energy efficiency, and safety. These challenges play to ADI's strengths in high-speed connectivity and power solutions designed to support functional safety requirements. L2+ autonomous driving systems remain relatively early in their global adoption, and as the industry progresses toward higher levels of autonomy, we expect content opportunities for ADI to continue to increase. In the past year, design and growth across our GMSL, A2B, and functionally safe power solutions underscores our substantial role in enabling the vehicle of tomorrow.

We saw a strong increase in designs for battery management solutions, which we expect to grow in the coming year and beyond as EV adoption increases. Not surprisingly, our data center business was our fastest-growing market in fiscal 2026, both from a revenue and design-in perspective. Robust investments in AI infrastructure are creating enormous challenges around two of the physical bottlenecks to scaling AI: moving exponentially more data and efficiently delivering unprecedented power loads. ADI is well-positioned to address both. In the networking domain, our optical control technology keeps electro-optical systems precisely tuned across everything from pluggables to OCS, so that every packet of light is accurate, stable, and efficient.

As you know, data center power has become one of the most significant constraints to AI advancement, as increasing rack and processor densities are fundamentally changing how power is converted, controlled, protected, and delivered. Customers are choosing ADI to help ensure that every watt used in the data center is available for computation and maximum impact. As the resulting thermodynamic challenges grow with increasing power density, liquid cooling is shifting from an option to a requirement. Customers are turning to ADI to translate physical signals, such as temperature, flow, leakage, and coolant health, into actionable intelligence, which is creating a new differentiated content opportunity.

Overall, we believe our data center revenues will continue to be one of the faster-growing businesses in 2027 and beyond. Finally, continued demand at the premium end of the consumer market overcame memory headwinds to drive double-digit growth in revenue and design activity across premium handsets, wearables, hearables, and gaming segments, which positions ADI for continued diversified growth in this sector in 2027 and beyond. In closing, FY 2026 demonstrated what makes ADI different. We are built to define and capture new waves of opportunity as we compound the businesses underpinning our resilience through cycles.

We leverage a six-decade culture of curiosity and cutting-edge innovation to continuously advance the state of the art at the electrophysical interface, a boundary that is increasingly central to the advance of technology's most valuable applications. Our customers increasingly choose ADI as a strategic partner for our applications, domain expertise, scope of high-performance analog software and AI capabilities, and differentiated hybrid manufacturing strategy. As we enter 2027, we continue to invest with discipline to further enhance and extend the value we can deliver to our customers and shareholders alike in the years ahead. With that, I'll turn it over to Rich.

Richard C. Puccio Jr.:Thank you, Vince, and let me add my welcome to our fourth quarter earnings call. I'll start with a brief overview of our full year fiscal 2026 financial performance. Revenue for the year came in at $15.2 billion, up 38% from fiscal 2025, reflecting broad-based strength across the business. Gross margin finished at 72.9%, up 360 basis points, driven by mix, utilization, and higher revenue. Operating margin finished at 49.5%, up 760 basis points, reflecting gross margin fall-through and strong operating leverage. Earnings per share increased 68% to $13.05. Turning to the fourth quarter, revenue came in toward the high end of our outlook at $4.37 billion, growing 9% sequentially and 42% year-over-year.

Industrial represented 50% of our fourth quarter revenue, finishing up 11% sequentially and 55% year-over-year. Ongoing cyclical momentum, along with secular demand in the AI infrastructure and defense markets, resulted in broad-based growth, including record results in aerospace and defense, ATE, and electronic test and measurement. For the full year, industrial grew 51%, reflecting the depth and breadth of our business, with all of our industrial sectors seeing accelerating double-digit growth. Aerospace and defense, ATE, and electronic test and measurement reached new highs for the year. Automotive represented 24% of quarterly revenue, finishing up 5% sequentially and 21% year-over-year.

We saw continued growth for our leading connectivity, audio processing, and power solutions, as well as a notable pickup in demand for our battery management systems. For the full year, automotive increased by 12%, driven by continued content and share gains in next-generation ADAS and infotainment systems, despite the backdrop of lower vehicle sales. Additionally, BMS revenue returned to full-year growth after two years of decline. Communications represented 16% of quarterly revenue, finishing up 8% sequentially and 81% year-over-year. Our data center business now represents 83% of comms, or 13% of total sales, growing more than 100% year-on-year for the second consecutive quarter, fueled by AI-driven demand.

Wireless revenue was up double digits year over year for the fifth straight quarter. For the full year, communications increased 74% and was our fastest-growing market for a second consecutive year, reflecting our growing presence in AI infrastructure and a cyclical recovery in wireless. Consumer represented 10% of quarterly revenue, finishing up 7% sequentially and year over year, remaining resilient in the face of memory-related headwinds. For the full year, consumer increased 15%, with all applications growing double digits, driven by our exposure to high-end handsets, secularly growing wearables and hearables, and a notable acceleration in our prosumer business. Now on to the rest of the P&L.

Fourth quarter gross margin was 74.5%, up 200 basis points sequentially and 470 basis points year over year, driven predominantly by favorable mix and higher revenue. OpEx in the quarter was $972 million, resulting in an operating margin of 52.3%, up 230 basis points sequentially and 880 basis points year over year. Non-operating expenses finished at $37 million, lower than expected due to mark-to-market gains from strategic balance sheet investments. Our tax rate for the quarter was 12.3%. EPS was $4.06, up 18% sequentially and 80% year over year. Now I'd like to highlight a few items from our balance sheet and cash flow statements.

Cash and short-term investments finished the quarter at $5.2 billion, and our net leverage ratio decreased slightly to 0.8x. As planned, we built strategic die bank and finished goods buffers throughout the quarter. Inventory increased $152 million sequentially, with days of inventory increasing to 165. Channel inventory also increased as we are now back within our six to seven-week model. The investments we have made in inventory over the past two years have helped drive sustained above-seasonal growth and mitigate lead time expansion, especially for certain products where demand is exceeding supply. Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow was $6.2 billion, and CapEx was $0.7 billion, resulting in free cash flow of $5.5 billion, or 36% of revenue.

Over the same period, we returned $5.4 billion to shareholders via dividends and share repurchase, in line with our commitment to return 100% of free cash flow over the long term. Now moving on to our first quarter 2027 outlook. Revenue is expected to be $4.4 billion, ± $150 million. Operating margin at the midpoint is expected to be 50.5%, ±100 basis points. Non-operating expense is expected to be roughly $90 million. Our tax rate is expected to be 12%-14%, and based on these inputs, adjusted EPS is expected to be $3.82, ±$0.20. Turning to capital investment.

We have executed well against our manufacturing expansion plans laid out at our Investor Day in 2022, building the capacity to support the high end of our 7%-10% long-term growth model. We are also well-positioned from a capacity standpoint to support sustained above-seasonal growth through fiscal 2027. Looking past 2027, while considering our momentum and the strong pipeline execution Vince referenced earlier, our confidence in future growth has risen. In order to capitalize on our potential, we are expanding our capacity further and currently expect fiscal 2027 CapEx to be approximately $1.6 billion-$1.9 billion.

Even with this higher investment, we expect fiscal 2027 free cash flow to increase meaningfully, and our commitment to return 100% of free cash flow over the long term is unchanged. In closing, fiscal 2026 caps one of the strongest growth years in ADI's history. We achieved record revenue, profitability, and earnings per share while generating more than $5 billion of free cash flow. We achieved these results while continuing to invest in the businesses and the innovation that we believe will fuel our future success. As we look ahead, we believe we are well-positioned to build on this momentum, supported by the strength of our business model and our track record of disciplined operational execution.

But also, if I look at the new products in our pipeline, the products that we're bringing to market now, some of these products have very, very significant multiples over the older generation products. I think in terms of the intersection of many markets in which we have increasing strength, our ability to support the old legacy products with increasing ASPs, newer products with much higher ASPs. And what we pay a lot of attention to, Tore, is the pipeline. I mean, what do the order books tell us? Well, the order books tell us right now that POS bookings are significantly higher than POS billings.

And our customer wins in terms of our design and pipeline right across all the sectors, and I mentioned many of them in the earnings script here, are at a record level. In fact, our 2026 pipeline has compounded significantly beyond an already strong 2025 pipeline, which grew significantly beyond 2024. You put all those things together, I see, for example, also in the world of AI, we're at the beginning of the buildout of a very, very significant meta-technology that will change all other technologies. So, we'll continue to unpack that story for you as time progresses. But I'd say we've got a lot of idiosyncratic secular tailwinds and cyclical, particularly in the industrial market.

Tore Svanberg:Thank you.

Jeff Ambrosi:Thanks, Tore. And just to clarify, Richard's comment on, it was a capacity statement on being able to support above seasonal growth. It wasn't guidance for the year for fiscal 2027. We'll take our next caller, please.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question comes from Vivek Arya with Bank of America Securities. Your line is open.

Vivek Arya:Thanks for taking my questions. Actually, both related to just the near-term outlook. You are guiding the current quarter sort of flattish. It seems a little conservative relative, I think, when it's to several quarters of above seasonal growth. I am just curious, would you call this kind of seasonal, below seasonal? Just what you are seeing from a sequential segment perspective. And then one for, kind of related, for Rich on operating margins. I think you are guiding down 200 basis points almost sequentially. Just what are the puts and takes of gross margin and OpEx, and is there some indication there of how we should think about those metrics trending into 2027? That would be incredibly helpful.

Thank you.

Vincent T. Roche:Sure. Rich, why don't you?

Richard C. Puccio Jr.:Thanks, Vivek. I will start with your first question around the seasonality. But first, just as a backdrop, the upside to our Q4 midpoint was driven heavily by the industrial and automotive, while comms was a little bit weaker, driven by some sequential softness in the wireless piece. Data center, however, was as expected and was up double digits sequentially, and consumer was as expected. Now, if we look out at the Q1 market outlook, as we have guided, we are expecting it to grow modestly quarter over quarter, which actually is well above our Q1 seasonality. Typically, our Q1 would be down mid-single digits. So, I do think that we are guiding a strong above seasonal first quarter.

From an end market perspective, we expect communications to be up mid-single digits, obviously being led by the data center growth. Industrial is expected to be up low mid-single digits. Auto expected to be down low single digits, and consumer down 10%-15%. The other thing I would tell you is we would expect channel inventory to stay flattish, with weeks likely to fall. That is how I feel about our guide from a revenue perspective. On the gross margin side, obviously we came in better than expected, driven by higher revenue and favorable mix.

As I mentioned, I think I talked about this in last quarter's call, we shut down our fabs around the holidays, which we will do again this year. As a result, we see gross margin in Q1 moderating down to approximately 74%. If we flip forward as we work our way down to the Op margin piece, obviously we delivered a significant amount of leverage in fiscal 2026. Q4 operating margin was about 30 bps above midpoint of our guidance, almost entirely driven by gross margin favorability, as expenses were a bit higher than planned, driven by sales commissions.

We are also leaning in, as we have talked about, into AI and driving a little bit higher token and cloud costs in that period. When we look at Q1, we are anticipating OpEx to grow in the mid-single digits sequentially, driven by our continued growth in our investments. We will also have a full year, sorry, a full quarter of Alif Semiconductor in our expenses, which obviously puts some upward pressure on the expense. However, and I think it is an important point, for the year, we continue to target OpEx growth at roughly half of the rate of revenue growth, and we do see continued operating leverage for the full year.

Jeff Ambrosi:Thank you, Vivek. Take our next caller, please.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question comes from James (Jim) Schneider with Goldman Sachs. Your line is open.

James (Jim) Schneider:Good morning. Thanks for taking my question. With respect to the CapEx investments you're making to expand capacity, can you maybe give us a sense, once those investments have been made this year, what revenue level you can support with the new capacity? Then maybe separately speak to any kind of constraints or bottlenecks you're seeing on the foundry side for those products which are made external to ADI. Thank you.

Richard C. Puccio Jr.:Thanks, Jim. First, a couple of starter points. The billion-dollar step-up essentially that I talked about in 2027 versus 2026, one important point is a chunk of that will be eligible for meaningful tax credits under the CHIPS Act. We will get some offset in our depreciation going forward and also get some offset in the amount of cash flow net that goes out the door. The way to think about the investment we're making, big piece of it is going to go towards clean room expansion at our European and U.S. sites. These are places where we already have available space within existing fabs, and we're also investing in back-end test and assembly capacity.

I do expect CapEx for these projects will decline as we move into 2028, and that will put us back down into our long-term CapEx model of 4%-6% of revenue. I do expect that we'll start to see some of the new capacity come online in stages, starting as early as, for us, Q1 2028, which gives us significantly more supply for our highest demand nodes and products. Obviously, really important positioning us for sustained future growth. I would say from a constraints perspective, frankly, I think it's tight everywhere. It's tight in internal fabs, back-end, OSAT, foundry. Right now, it's an industry-wide dynamic.

I would say for us, we're working really hard to sort of de-bottleneck and unlock incremental supply everywhere we can. I think I've talked in prior quarters that essentially on a weekly basis, we're adding incremental capability and capacity as tools are coming online from purchases we started making upwards of nine months ago, just to give some perspective on how long the team has been working on building up supply. Obviously, we've been able to demonstrate what we've been doing there with our ability to supply above seasonal demand throughout this past year, and we expect we can continue to do the same into 2027.

Vincent T. Roche:Yeah, just a couple of additional pieces of color. I think certainly over the past six months or so, I would say packaging, assembly has been the primary choke point.
